top_role: Executive Director and CEO, The Permanente Medical Group (and CEO of Mid-Atlantic Permanente Medical Group)

journey.year_note: "Within five years" of the affiliation; affiliation year not given.

journey.quote: Within five years, the Mid-Atlantic had actually replaced TPMG as number one, and they were able to do it while growing their market share

journey.year_note: During his CEO tenure; no year given.

journey.quote: We had 12,000 physicians in total, and over 2,000 of them went through leadership training. And I don't mean, you know, a lunchtime session. I'm talking about a two-year program

journey.year_note: After 18 years as CEO, which he began in 1999.

journey.quote: And after doing the CEO role for 18 years, I wanted to be able to change health care for 300 million Americans. And there's no way to reach people except through the media.

journey.quote: I teach both in the medical school at Stanford and the business school at Stanford, and I try to bring both of these perspectives together

retellable.title: The man behind the mask
retellable.summary: On a trip to Mexico with Stanford's plastic surgery chairman, Pearl operated on an adult who had hidden his cleft lip behind a mask all his life. The 90-minute operation changed the man's life and turned Pearl toward plastic surgery.
retellable.quote: I can still remember the first patient, an individual, an adult, actually, who had spent his whole life with a mask over his face. He didn't want anyone to see the cleft lip
retellable.why: Shows how one patient encounter set a career's direction.

retellable.title: Facing down the health plan in 1998
retellable.summary: On taking the CEO role, Pearl met a health plan head who threatened to break the medical group's contracts. Pearl warned that every emergency room would close and the plan would go bankrupt, and the plan backed down.
retellable.quote: And I said, I don't think you're going to do that, because as soon as you do that, every emergency room is going to close and the costs are going to be so great that you're going to go bankrupt.
retellable.why: A vivid moment in the medical group-health plan partnership's history.

retellable.title: From Motel6 to Johns Hopkins recruits
retellable.summary: Mid-Atlantic physician recruitment had been held on Sunday afternoons at a Motel6 with chips and salsa. Pearl's team moved it to a fine Baltimore restaurant, drawing 80 Johns Hopkins attendees and 20 new physicians.
retellable.quote: the way they did physician recruitment was on a Sunday afternoon at a Motel6 where they'd have some chips and salsa, and the first thing we did is we went to Baltimore
retellable.why: Concrete, memorable illustration of brand-building in a struggling region.

retellable.title: The paper that predicted failure
retellable.summary: A friend at Berkeley's business school wrote an A-graded strategy paper concluding KP's shift to quality and service differentiation would fail. Pearl says the outcome not only matched but greatly exceeded the community.
retellable.quote: And the paper was an analysis of our decision to shift the strategy. And this paper she got an A on, concluded that we would not be successful.
retellable.why: Captures the risk and doubt behind the 1998 strategy shift.
